location.name: Crowe's office
location.asset: Edith Voss has come about her brother. Read his hour to her in this room, she says, and leave the floor at berth four shut. She will be back at midnight.

charview.text: Edith waits in the client's chair, her gloves in her lap.
charview.conversation: "Thomas kept the tide at the harbour office. He went down to berth four for his hour, and he did not come up."
"There is a trap in the shack floor at berth four. Whatever you hear under it, leave it shut."
"The Harbor Hotel. Grayhaven 3071, if you must. I will be back in this chair at midnight."

location.asset: She stands, buttons her gloves, and goes. The door lets the rain in and shuts on it.

view.text: The desk. The folder on the blotter, the telephone, the green lamp.
The window side. Rain on the glass, and her chair, empty.
The door side. Your hat on the hook, CROWE backwards on the glass.

location.asset:
Thomas Voss, tide clerk, twenty-eight. Berth four, the trawler Patience. A photograph is clipped inside.
In the margin her pencil reads: the hour, to her, in this room. Not to the water. Not in the rain.
The exchange tries the harbour office for you. The operator says it rang off at the turn of the tide and has not answered since. Grayhaven 214.
Green glass, a dry blotter, a room with a door that shuts. This is the room she meant.
Across the rain a man stands under the streetlamp, too still for the weather. An olive coat, brass buttons. Your hand finds the latch. The cobbles are empty.
Rain on the glass. The lamp over empty cobbles. Nothing stands there now.
The seat is still warm. She left the smell of rain and violets, and nothing else.
Your hand is on the knob. You have not read her folder yet. The job is on the desk.
location.ending: You hang up your hat and call it a night. In the morning the folder is still on the desk, and Thomas Voss is a wet line on a washed board.

view.text: Midnight. Edith is in the chair. Her folder is on the blotter and the window is rain.

charview.label: Edith
charview.text: She does not ask. She waits.
charview.conversation: "Once for the harbour, once for me. He always did."
She takes it, looks, and gives it back. "Keep it until it is done."
"He cut that when he was nineteen, the first time his name went on the board. It is not his name any more."
"On the folder," she says. "Here. Not to the glass."

location.asset: The lamp burns over empty cobbles. Rain works the glass. The hour has not been spoken in this room yet.
She opens the locket for you. The photograph is the face from the folder, younger, dry. "He wrote me which room," she says. "I did not understand it until tonight."
She opens the locket and keeps it open a moment longer. "That peg in your coat is his. The name in the ledger is the one that matters now."
location.ending: You read Thomas's hour onto her folder. Edith closes the locket. The streetlamp stays empty, and the floor you left shut does not answer.
You read the hour here. Edith closes the locket. Outside, the rain is only rain, and the floor at berth four stays shut.
You read his hour to the wet glass. The man under the lamp steps in close, and the latch rises under a hand that is not yours.
